title: Unit-normalized closed comparisons on finite total complexes
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $A$ a sheaf of commutative rings on $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], and use module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] with inverse-image coefficient rings and the actual module inverse and direct images [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. Use the canonical unit-normalized adjunctions [def-sfb-proetale-unit-normalized-adjunction]. Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ and $i_a:Z_a\hookrightarrow X$, $1\leq a\leq m$, be closed immersions [def-weil-closed-immersion], with each $i_a$ factoring through $i$. Let $M$ range over $A$-module sheaves. Assume their complementary open immersions [def-weil-open-immersion] are quasi-compact morphisms [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Assume $m\geq1$; no covering hypothesis is needed. For a nonempty subset $J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,m\}$ let $Z_J$ be the scheme-theoretic intersection (the iterated fibre product over $X$ [def-pc-fibre-product]), and put $E_J=i_{J,*}i_J^*$ and $E_Z=i_*i^*$. For $J\subseteq L$, let $r_{J,L}:E_J\to E_L$ be the actual unit of $Z_L\hookrightarrow Z_J$ pushed to $X$, with inverse-image composition identifications; define $r_{Z,J}$ similarly. Write $D^{-1}(M)=E_Z(M)$, $D^p(M)=\bigoplus_{|J|=p+1}E_J(M)$ for $0\leq p<m$, and $D^p=0$ otherwise. The proposed differential is
$$ (dc)_{(a_0<\cdots<a_{p+1})}=\sum_{t=0}^{p+1}(-1)^t r_{L\setminus\{a_t\},L}(c_{L\setminus\{a_t\}}),\qquad d^{-1}=(r_{Z,\{a\}})_a. $$
Let $g:X'\to X$ be a scheme morphism, $A'=g^{-1}A$, and let $E'_T$ be the corresponding closed restriction on $X'$ for $T\in\{Z\}\cup\{Z_J:J\ne\varnothing\}$. Use the canonical coefficient-composition identifications. Suppose given natural isomorphisms
$$c_T:g^*E_T\xrightarrow{\sim}E'_Tg^*,\qquad c_T\,g^*(\eta_T)=\eta'_T g^*$$
for every such $T$, including $T=Z$. These unit equations alone imply that every square of restriction faces commutes. The degreewise direct sums of the $c_{Z_J}$ give a natural isomorphism of augmented row complexes, with $c_Z$ in degree $-1$.
For every bounded-below complex $K$, let $C(K)$ and $C'(g^*K)$ be the finite totals of the nonnegative rows, with differential $d_D+(-1)^p d_K$ and augmentations $\alpha$ and $\alpha'$. There is a unique natural chain isomorphism
$$\tau_K:g^*C(K)\xrightarrow{\sim}C'(g^*K)$$
whose component on every diagonal inclusion is the componentwise direct sum of $c_{Z_J}$, namely
$$\tau_K^n\,g^*(\iota_{p,q})=\iota'_{p,q}\,(\bigoplus_{|J|=p+1}c_{Z_J,K^q}),\qquad p+q=n.$$
It satisfies $\tau_K\,g^*\alpha_K=\alpha'_{g^*K}c_{Z,K}$. If both augmentations are quasi-isomorphisms, localization $Q$ in the ordinary derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] satisfies
$$Q(\tau_K)=Q(\alpha'_{g^*K})\,Q(c_{Z,K})\,Q(g^*\alpha_K)^{-1}.$$
These equations are identities of natural transformations, preserved by compatible morphisms, iterated pullback comparisons, automorphisms, and small parameter diagrams. A parameter diagram means a functor from a small category into the displayed data, with all comparisons natural on that category. No existence of closed base change for an arbitrary $g$ is asserted without the supplied unit-compatible comparisons.

proof.text: For every nonempty $J$, the closed-immersion product lemma (applied to $Z_a\to X$ and $Z_b\to X$ over the base $X$, with $X\times_XX=X$, and inductively on $|J|$) shows that $i_J:Z_J\to X$ is a closed immersion; the same holds for the pulled-back family $Z'_J=Z_J\times_XX'$ in $X'$. As a set $Z_J$ is $\bigcap_{a\in J}Z_a$ (the fibre product of closed immersions is the preimage of one closed subscheme in the other), so the complement of $Z_J$ is the finite union of the complements of $Z_a$, $a\in J$. Over each affine open of $X$ these are quasi-compact spaces, so their finite union is quasi-compact; hence its open immersion is quasi-compact. The same holds for $Z$. The ringed open-closed lemma therefore makes every actual unit $\eta_{T,M}:M\to E_T(M)$ an epimorphism. With inverse-image coefficients $g^*$ is exact by the geometric-inverse-image lemma; exact functors preserve epimorphisms, so $g^*\eta_{T,M}$ is epimorphic. All complements after base change are quasi-compact by quasi-compact base change. Apply the signed-restriction lemma to the original and pulled-back families to obtain their additive augmented row complexes. Its hypotheses require no covering.

proof.text:
The unit identity in the signed-restriction lemma, applied also with ambient closed support $Z_J$ and singleton subfamily $Z_L$, gives $r_{J,L}\eta_J=\eta_L$; it also gives $r_{Z,J}\eta_Z=\eta_J$. For $J\subseteq L$ compare $c_Lg^*r_{J,L}$ and $r'_{J,L}c_J$. Precomposing with $g^*\eta_J$ gives, respectively,
$$c_Lg^*(r_{J,L}\eta_J)=c_Lg^*\eta_L=\eta'_Lg^*,\qquad r'_{J,L}c_Jg^*\eta_J=r'_{J,L}\eta'_Jg^*=\eta'_Lg^*.$$
Cancel the epimorphism from step 1 to obtain the face square. Replacing $J$ by $Z$ gives the augmentation-face square. These are equations of natural transformations since the calculation holds at every module with the supplied natural $c_T$.

proof.text: An additive functor preserves finite biproducts directly from their equations: applying it to $\pi_a\iota_b=\delta_{ab}$ and $\sum_a\iota_a\pi_a=1$ gives the same biproduct equations. Thus identify $g^*D^p(M)$ with $\bigoplus_{|J|=p+1}g^*E_J(M)$. The sum $b^p_M=\bigoplus_Jc_{J,M}$ is invertible, with inverse the sum of $c_{J,M}^{-1}$. Each matrix entry of $b^{p+1}g^*d^p-d'^pb^p$ is the signed difference of the two face composites proved equal in step 2, hence zero. In degree $-1$ use $b^{-1}=c_Z$; its chain equation is exactly the augmentation-face squares. This proves the asserted natural augmented-row isomorphism.

proof.text: Put $B^{p,q}=D^p(K^q)$ for $0\leq p<m$ and zero otherwise, with commuting differentials $d_D$ and $D^p(d_K)$; the signed-restriction lemma gives their commutation. Naturality of each $c_J$ at $d_K^q$ and step 2 make $b^{p,q}$ a componentwise invertible bicomplex map $g^*B\to B'$, where $B'^{p,q}=D'^p(g^*K^q)$. For each total degree $n$ only $m$ horizontal indices can contribute. These diagonal coproducts exist as finite biproducts and are preserved by $g^*$ by step 3 (the remaining summands are zero). Apply the additive-total-comparison lemma to identify $g^*C(K)\cong\operatorname{Tot}(g^*B)$ with its stated diagonal inclusions. Define the map from this total to $\operatorname{Tot}(B')$ on each $(p,q)$ summand by $b^{p,q}$. Its chain equation on that summand is the sum of the horizontal equation and $(-1)^p$ times the vertical equation. Summing the inverses gives its chain inverse. Their composite is $\tau_K$, and the inclusion identity of the total-comparison lemma gives exactly the displayed characterization of $\tau_K^n$. Equality on all diagonal inclusions proves uniqueness and naturality in chain maps $K\to L$.

proof.text: In degree $n$ the augmentation lands only in $(0,n)$. The characterization of $\tau_K$ reduces its augmentation square to $b^0g^*d^{-1}=d'^{-1}c_Z$, proved in step 3. Thus $\tau_Kg^*\alpha_K=\alpha'_{g^*K}c_{Z,K}$ as chain maps. Suppose both augmentations are quasi-isomorphisms. Exactness of $g^*$ and its natural homology comparison imply that $g^*\alpha_K$ is a quasi-isomorphism. Localization sends it to an invertible map. Apply $Q$ to the chain equality and compose on the right by $Q(g^*\alpha_K)^{-1}$ to obtain exactly the asserted derived identity. Here $c_{Z,K}$ is a chain isomorphism by naturality at each differential, not a newly chosen derived comparison.

proof.text: For a compatible morphism of the displayed data, the naturality square for $\tau$ can be tested on every diagonal inclusion: it is the corresponding stipulated square for $c_J$, followed by the target inclusion. The augmentation case is the square for $c_Z$. For successive pullbacks $X''\xrightarrow{h}X'\xrightarrow{g}X$, the component comparison is $c^h_{T'}\,h^*c^g_T$, using coefficient composition identifications; its unit equation follows by applying the two supplied unit equations. Any separately supplied unit-normalized comparison for $gh$ equals this composite: precompose their difference with the epimorphic $(gh)^*\eta_T$ and cancel as in step 2. The two proposed total maps now agree on every diagonal inclusion, so uniqueness in step 4 proves the iterated-pullback equation. Identities and associativity follow by the same inclusion test. Apply the morphism calculation to automorphisms, or objectwise to each arrow of any small parameter category. Inversion of natural isomorphisms and functoriality of $Q$ preserve these commuting squares and the equality in step 5. Thus all equations have the claimed natural-transformation compatibility.
